proposal.title: Disable CF fill-value masking metadata on fully written data chunks
proposal.hypothesis: Operational evidence shows the consumer benchmark is warm-cache shuffled full-field tensor access over 28 samples, while provider/cache changes cannot improve consumer_samples_per_second. The current uncompressed one-sample full-field chunks minimize decompression, so remaining read overhead can come from xarray's CF decode path checking float data against default missing-value metadata. If published data arrays explicitly omit _FillValue metadata while all chunks remain fully materialized and validation/array paths/dimensions/selectors stay unchanged, consumer reads should avoid per-chunk missing-value masking work and increase consumer_samples_per_second without changing semantic float values.
proposal.expected_tradeoffs: Output bytes may change only by a few metadata bytes, and materialization time should be similar. This does not target compression ratio or provider acquisition; if the evaluator already bypasses CF mask checks, the throughput effect may be neutral.

edits.rationale: Keeping fully written uncompressed chunks but suppressing default floating _FillValue metadata can reduce xarray/Zarr decode-side masking checks during warm full-field reads, without changing names, coordinates, selector dimensions, chunk layout, or values.

proposal.validation_plan: Run the evaluator command unchanged. Confirm contract correctness, semantic equivalence, provenance/security, and rerun safety still pass; verify frozen Zarr v3 paths and selector coordinates remain unchanged; compare consumer_samples_per_second against the current 209.7 samples/s baseline.
